newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end firmer but gains pared on U.S..
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end firmer but gains pared on U.S..

text.p: Italian shares ended Friday's session in positive territory but earlier gains were reduced in line with falls on Wall Street and other European bourses after stronger than expected U.S. producer price and retails sales data.
The All-share Mibtel index closed 0.64 pct up at 12,079 after a session high of 12,149. The Mib30 blue chip index ended 0.84 pct up at 17,926 after an 18,038 peak.

"The U.S. data revived fears about a likely rise in U.S. interest rates but on the Italian front, after the government's brush with crisis this week, there's a feeling the focus will return to the fairly good fundamentals here," one trader said.

As factors supporting the Milan market, operators cited falling inflation renewing expectations of a Bank of Italy official interest rate cut before too long as well as strong buying on bourse futures in Friday's session and strength in blue chip stock Fiat, up 2.29 percent at 5,585 lire, on 1997 prospects given the jump in German Volkswagen's share price on a higher profits outlook.
Olivetti, the most traded stock, slipped 0.48 percent to 562.8 lire after bouncing earlier when it denied capital increase plans.
Telecoms were mixed with Stet off 0.12 pct at 7,780, TIM up 1.58 pct at 4,898 and Telecom Italia off 0.45 pct at 4,401.

Yellow pages publishing company Seat fell sharply on the Milan bourse on press reports that candidates in line to bid for the group had made much lower final offers than expected. It ended 4.97 pct off at 546.7 lire.
Insurance and financial services group Mediolanum closed 1.49 percent firmer at 15,436 following a positive analyst meeting in London on Thursday, traders said.
The June FIB bourse index contract was 85 points firmer at 17,890.
Total traded volume was estimated up at around 800 billion lire against 563 billion lire on Thursday.
